To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human polymerase gene is located on chromosome 1, is regulated by cAMP and phorbol esters, and is expressed as a single mRNA species in all tissues tested.
poly(ADPRP) is encoded by a single copy gene, and that its expression is regulated by cAMP and phorbol esters.

the promoter region of the polymerases gene has been isolated, that the promoter region lacks typical transcriptional regulator elements, that the region up to position -99 in relation to transcriptional initiation site has promoter activity, that expression of polymerase gene is stimulated by cAMP and phorbol esters in HeLa cells, that the polymerase gene appears to be unique in genomic DNA, and that the promoter region may contain two potential Sp1 and three putative Ap2 binding elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and expression of a gene encoding the poly(ADPribose) polymerase.
the cloning and sequencing of the human gene for poly (ADP-ribo) polymerase.
the molecular cloning and characterization of the gene encoding poly(ADP ribosyltransferase) (EC 2.4.2.30).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the polymerase gene has a promoter region, which lacks TATA and CAATA boxes but contains two potential SpI binding sites and three AP-2 binding sites, and that the expression of the gene is regulated by cAMP and phorbol esters.
this gene is not a member of the AP-2 family, and that its promoter region lacks a typical TATA and CAATA box.
the human poly(ADP-Rib) polymerase gene is regulated by the same mechanisms as the c-fos gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polymerase is a unique gene whose transcription is controlled by cAMP and phorbol esters.
the poly(ADPRP) gene is a member of the family of immediate early genes and is regulated by the cAMP-dependent pathway.
the poly(ADPribose) polymerase (PARP) gene is regulated by cAMP and phorbol esters, which may be important for the control of cell proliferation and/or differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have cloned the promoter of poly (ADP-ribo) polymerase and that this promoter is responsive to cAMP and phorbol esters.
the polymerase gene promoter region is not only devoid of typical transcriptional control sequences but is also highly sensitive to the presence of cAMP and phorbol esters.
the poly(ADPR) synthetase gene is a unique gene, and it has a promoter region.
